show_hn.story_text: Making models better at formal verification will help push the boundaries of math research and significantly reduce the number of bugs in our code. Recently, training models on RL environments (tasks paired with verifiers that reward correct solutions) has driven big gains in model performance, and proofs are unusually easy to verify. Here we introduce TheoremSmith, a pipeline for generating synthetic formal verification environments. It reliably creates multi-hour, frontier-difficulty tasks and can scale throughput effectively. I'd appreciate any feedback, especially on ways models could still cheat the verifier, and on whether synthetic tasks like these are likely to help on real proofs. show_hn.title: Show HN: Spared – self-hosted Workers and Durable Objects for Rust apps
show_hn.story_text: Hi HN, I wanted something like workerd + celld for untrusted Rust apps and couldn’t find anything that quite fit.  That said, I got a lot of inspiration from workerd, celld, spin, and wasmcloud. spared (spare-dee) runs Rust apps + SQLite in isolated WASM sandboxes. It lets you run many apps per server, and by packaging SQLite inside the sandbox, you get better isolation than running it on the host. This opens the door to running untrusted code on a single machine. It's open source and runs on any VPS. It's still early, and there's still a lot to build, but it feels like it's at a good place to share. Let me know what you think.
